title: Control-plane warm-standby + per-tenant leaky-throttle for safe cross-region upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce blast radius and maintain SLOs during cross-region control-plane upgrades for Dedicated/Private customers by introducing a warm-standby control-plane pattern plus per-tenant adaptive leaky-bucket throttles. This work alters upgrade orchestration, admission control, and telemetry so rolling upgrades can proceed with measurable safety margins and automated load-shedding if per-tenant budgets are exceeded.
acceptance_criteria: Warm-standby control plane instances can be promoted in <60s without requiring tenant re-registration
Per-tenant leaky-bucket throttles enforce configurable token rates and burst windows and are attachable to control-plane ingress
Upgrade orchestration will schedule region-by-region with automated burst windows and SLO-aware gate checks and will abort or roll back if control-plane tail latency SLOs exceed threshold
Simulated tenant surge tests show <3% sustained SLO breach for high-priority tenants and graceful degradation for low-priority tenants
Playbook for incident response and rollback exists in Confluence with runbook steps, dashboard links, and escape hatches
success_metrics: Reduction in upgrade-related tenant incidents by >=75% vs prior 3 months
Mean control-plane P99 latency during upgrades stays within 1.4x baseline
Automated canary promotions succeed in >=95% of rehearsals
tasks: Design API for attaching per-tenant throttle policies to control-plane routes
Implement warm-standby control-plane lifecycle (sync, health, promotion)
Integrate SLO gate checks into upgrade orchestrator and add automated abort/rollback
Add telemetry: per-tenant admission metrics, token consumption, throttle drops, and upgrade-phase latency
Create synthetic rehearsals (chaos + traffic generator) and QA scenarios
Confluence playbook, runbooks, and incident drill schedule
Docs: runtime release notes and admin guide for customers on configuring tenant headroom
